question: Which word is closest in meaning to “elusive”?
fr: Quel mot a le sens le plus proche de « elusive » (insaisissable) ?

explain.fr: « elusive » et « hard to catch » ont un sens proche : insaisissable.
explain.en: “elusive” and “hard to catch” have a similar meaning.

question: Which word is closest in meaning to “exacerbate”?
fr: Quel mot a le sens le plus proche de « exacerbate » (aggraver) ?

explain.fr: « exacerbate » et « aggravate » ont un sens proche : aggraver.
explain.en: “exacerbate” and “aggravate” have a similar meaning.

question: Which word is closest in meaning to “thwart”?
fr: Quel mot a le sens le plus proche de « thwart » (contrecarrer) ?

explain.fr: « thwart » et « frustrate » ont un sens proche : contrecarrer.
explain.en: “thwart” and “frustrate” have a similar meaning.

question: Which word is closest in meaning to “squander”?
fr: Quel mot a le sens le plus proche de « squander » (gaspiller) ?

explain.fr: « squander » et « waste » ont un sens proche : gaspiller.
explain.en: “squander” and “waste” have a similar meaning.

question: Which word is closest in meaning to “ubiquitous”?
fr: Quel mot a le sens le plus proche de « ubiquitous » (omniprésent) ?

explain.fr: « ubiquitous » et « omnipresent » ont un sens proche : omniprésent.
explain.en: “ubiquitous” and “omnipresent” have a similar meaning.

question: Which word is closest in meaning to “wary”?
fr: Quel mot a le sens le plus proche de « wary » (méfiant) ?

explain.fr: « wary » et « cautious » ont un sens proche : méfiant.
explain.en: “wary” and “cautious” have a similar meaning.

question: Which word is closest in meaning to “tenuous”?
fr: Quel mot a le sens le plus proche de « tenuous » (ténu) ?

explain.fr: « tenuous » et « weak » ont un sens proche : ténu.
explain.en: “tenuous” and “weak” have a similar meaning.

question: Her ___ was legendary. (GENEROUS)
fr: Sa générosité était légendaire.

explain.fr: À partir de « generous », on forme « generosity ».
explain.en: From “generous”, we form “generosity”.

question: The ___ of the evidence surprised the jury. (ADMIT)
fr: La recevabilité des preuves a surpris le jury.

explain.fr: À partir de « admit », on forme « admissibility ».
explain.en: From “admit”, we form “admissibility”.

say: The admissibility of the evidence surprised the jury.

question: The policy had ___ consequences. (FORESEE)
fr: La politique a eu des conséquences imprévues.

explain.fr: À partir de « foresee », on forme « unforeseen ».
explain.en: From “foresee”, we form “unforeseen”.

question: The scheme proved ___. (SUSTAIN)
fr: Le projet s'est révélé insoutenable.

explain.fr: À partir de « sustain », on forme « unsustainable ».
explain.en: From “sustain”, we form “unsustainable”.

question: He was praised for his ___. (RESOURCE)
fr: Il a été salué pour son ingéniosité.

explain.fr: À partir de « resource », on forme « resourcefulness ».
explain.en: From “resource”, we form “resourcefulness”.

say: He was praised for his resourcefulness.

question: The ___ of the two accounts is striking. (SIMILAR)
fr: La ressemblance entre les deux récits est frappante.

explain.fr: À partir de « similar », on forme « similarity ».
explain.en: From “similar”, we form “similarity”.

say: The similarity of the two accounts is striking.

question: The costs were ___ high. (PROHIBIT)
fr: Les coûts étaient d'un niveau prohibitif.

explain.fr: À partir de « prohibit », on forme « prohibitively ».
explain.en: From “prohibit”, we form “prohibitively”.

question: The film's ending was ___. (ANTICLIMAX)
fr: La fin du film était décevante.

explain.fr: À partir de « anticlimax », on forme « anticlimactic ».
explain.en: From “anticlimax”, we form “anticlimactic”.

question: ___ it may, we must press on.
fr: Quoi qu'il en soit, nous devons continuer.

explain.fr: Formule figée au subjonctif : Be that as it may.
explain.en: Fixed subjunctive formula: Be that as it may.

say: Be that as it may, we must press on.

question: Come ___ may, I will not give up.
fr: Quoi qu'il arrive, je n'abandonnerai pas.

explain.fr: Formule figée : Come what may.
explain.en: Fixed formula: Come what may.

say: Come what may, I will not give up.

question: Far ___ it from me to interfere.
fr: Loin de moi l'idée de m'en mêler.

explain.fr: Formule figée : Far be it from me to…
explain.en: Fixed formula: Far be it from me to…

say: Far be it from me to interfere.

question: Suffice it ___ that he was not pleased.
fr: Disons simplement qu'il n'était pas content.

explain.fr: Formule figée : Suffice it to say (that)…
explain.en: Fixed formula: Suffice it to say (that)…

say: Suffice it to say that he was not pleased.

question: If need ___, we can work through the night.
fr: Si besoin est, nous pouvons travailler toute la nuit.

explain.fr: Subjonctif figé : if need be.
explain.en: Fixed subjunctive: if need be.

say: If need be, we can work through the night.

question: It is vital that the patient not ___ disturbed.
fr: Il est vital que le patient ne soit pas dérangé.

explain.fr: Subjonctif négatif : not + be (sans « do »).
explain.en: Negative subjunctive: not + be (no “do”).

say: It is vital that the patient not be disturbed.

question: The board demanded that the CEO ___ immediately.
fr: Le conseil a exigé que le PDG démissionne immédiatement.

explain.fr: demand that + verbe de base.
explain.en: demand that + base verb.

say: The board demanded that the CEO resign immediately.

question: ___ the proposal be rejected, we will appeal.
fr: Si la proposition devait être rejetée, nous ferions appel.

explain.fr: Should + sujet + verbe = if (soutenu).
explain.en: Should + subject + verb = if (formal).

say: Should the proposal be rejected, we will appeal.

question: ___ the plan to fail, who would take the blame?
fr: Si le plan échouait, qui en porterait la responsabilité ?

explain.fr: Were + sujet + to + verbe = if + sujet + were to…
explain.en: Were + subject + to + verb = if… were to.

say: Were the plan to fail, who would take the blame?

question: Try ___ might, he could not lift it.
fr: Il avait beau essayer, il ne pouvait pas le soulever.

explain.fr: Try as + sujet + might = avoir beau essayer.
explain.en: Try as + subject + might = however hard he tried.

say: Try as he might, he could not lift it.

question: Strange ___ it may seem, I enjoyed the exam.
fr: Aussi étrange que cela puisse paraître, l'examen m'a plu.

explain.fr: Adjectif + as / though + sujet + verbe = aussi… que.
explain.en: Adjective + as / though + subject + verb = however…

say: Strange as it may seem, I enjoyed the exam.

question: Only by working together ___ this crisis.
fr: Ce n'est qu'en travaillant ensemble que nous pourrons surmonter cette crise.

explain.fr: Only by + -ing en tête : inversion.
explain.en: Only by + -ing at the start: inversion.

say: Only by working together can we overcome this crisis.

question: Nowhere ___ more evident than in the capital.
fr: Nulle part le problème n'est plus évident que dans la capitale.

explain.fr: Nowhere en tête : inversion.
explain.en: Nowhere at the start: inversion.

say: Nowhere is the problem more evident than in the capital.

question: In no way ___ responsible for the delay.
fr: L'entreprise n'est en rien responsable du retard.

explain.fr: In no way en tête : inversion.
explain.en: In no way at the start: inversion.

say: In no way is the company responsible for the delay.

question: Not a word ___ during the entire ceremony.
fr: Il n'a pas dit un mot de toute la cérémonie.

explain.fr: Not a + nom en tête : inversion.
explain.en: Not a + noun at the start: inversion.

say: Not a word did he say during the entire ceremony.

question: Down ___ the rain.
fr: La pluie s'est abattue.

explain.fr: Adverbe de lieu en tête + verbe de mouvement : inversion verbe-sujet (style narratif).
explain.en: Place adverb at the start + verb of movement: verb-subject inversion (narrative style).

question: Here ___ the bus!
fr: Voilà le bus !

explain.fr: Here / There + verbe + nom : inversion (pas avec un pronom : Here it comes).
explain.en: Here / There + verb + noun: inversion (not with a pronoun: Here it comes).

question: So ___ the noise that we couldn't sleep.
fr: Le bruit était si fort que nous ne pouvions pas dormir.

explain.fr: So + adjectif + be + sujet.
explain.en: So + adjective + be + subject.

say: So loud was the noise that we couldn't sleep.

question: I'm not averse ___ the occasional glass of wine.
fr: Je ne suis pas contre un verre de vin de temps en temps.

explain.fr: averse to + -ing.
explain.en: averse to + -ing.

say: I'm not averse to having the occasional glass of wine.

question: She was on the verge ___ up when the call came.
fr: Elle était sur le point d'abandonner quand l'appel est arrivé.

explain.fr: on the verge of + -ing.
explain.en: on the verge of + -ing.

say: She was on the verge of giving up when the call came.

question: He made a point ___ everyone personally.
fr: Il a tenu à remercier chacun personnellement.

explain.fr: make a point of + -ing = tenir à.
explain.en: make a point of + -ing.

say: He made a point of thanking everyone personally.

question: It's no good ___ over spilt milk.
fr: Inutile de pleurer sur le lait renversé.

explain.fr: It's no good + -ing.
explain.en: It's no good + -ing.

say: It's no good crying over spilt milk.

question: ___ his age, he is remarkably fit.
fr: Compte tenu de son âge, il est remarquablement en forme.

explain.fr: Considering + nom = compte tenu de.
explain.en: Considering + noun.

say: Considering his age, he is remarkably fit.

question: ___ from the hill, the town looks tiny.
fr: Vue de la colline, la ville paraît minuscule.

explain.fr: Participe passé à sens passif en tête de phrase.
explain.en: Past participle with passive meaning at the start.

say: Seen from the hill, the town looks tiny.

question: ___ the letter, she burst into tears.
fr: Après avoir lu la lettre, elle a fondu en larmes.

explain.fr: Antériorité : Having + participe.
explain.en: Earlier action: Having + participle.

say: Having read the letter, she burst into tears.

question: The meeting ___, everyone went home.
fr: La réunion terminée, tout le monde est rentré.

explain.fr: Proposition absolue : nom + adjectif / participe (style soutenu).
explain.en: Absolute clause: noun + adjective / participle (formal).

say: The meeting over, everyone went home.

question: Weather ___, the match will take place on Sunday.
fr: Si le temps le permet, le match aura lieu dimanche.

explain.fr: Proposition absolue figée : weather permitting.
explain.en: Fixed absolute clause: weather permitting.

say: Weather permitting, the match will take place on Sunday.

question: You ___ well ask why we bothered.
fr: On peut bien se demander pourquoi nous nous sommes donné cette peine.

explain.fr: may well = avoir de bonnes raisons de.
explain.en: may well = have good reason to.

say: You may well ask why we bothered.

question: I ___ have thought she would accept.
fr: J'aurais pensé qu'elle accepterait.

explain.fr: would have thought = j'aurais cru.
explain.en: would have thought.

say: I would have thought she would accept.

question: You ___ have seen his face! It was priceless.
fr: Si tu avais vu sa tête ! C'était impayable.

explain.fr: should have seen = tu aurais dû voir (exclamation).
explain.en: should have seen (exclamation).

say: You should have seen his face! It was priceless.

question: He ___ not have known about the decision; nobody had told him.
fr: Il ne pouvait pas être au courant de la décision ; personne ne l'avait prévenu.

explain.fr: could not have + participe = impossibilité dans le passé.
explain.en: could not have + participle = past impossibility.

say: He could not have known about the decision; nobody had told him.

question: Who ___ have guessed that the shy boy would become a star?
fr: Qui aurait cru que ce garçon timide deviendrait une star ?

explain.fr: Who would have thought / guessed…?
explain.en: Who would have thought / guessed…?

say: Who would have guessed that the shy boy would become a star?

question: Need I ___ you that this is confidential?
fr: Ai-je besoin de vous rappeler que c'est confidentiel ?

explain.fr: need modal (soutenu) : Need I + verbe de base ?
explain.en: Modal “need” (formal): Need I + base verb?

say: Need I remind you that this is confidential?

question: I dare ___ you'll be hungry after the journey.
fr: J'imagine que tu auras faim après le voyage.

explain.fr: I dare say = je suppose (expression figée).
explain.en: I dare say = I suppose (fixed expression).

say: I dare say you'll be hungry after the journey.

question: ___ the two sisters, Emma is by far the more ambitious.
fr: Des deux sœurs, Emma est de loin la plus ambitieuse.

explain.fr: Comparaison entre deux : Of the two…, the more…
explain.en: Comparison of two: Of the two…, the more…

say: Of the two sisters, Emma is by far the more ambitious.

question: There were ___ few volunteers that the event was canceled.
fr: Il y avait si peu de bénévoles que l'événement a été annulé.

explain.fr: so + few / little / many / much.
explain.en: so + few / little / many / much.

say: There were so few volunteers that the event was canceled.

question: It was ___ chaos that nobody knew what to do.
fr: C'était un tel chaos que personne ne savait quoi faire.

explain.fr: such + nom indénombrable (sans « a »).
explain.en: such + uncountable noun (no “a”).

say: It was such chaos that nobody knew what to do.

question: ___ a word did she utter.
fr: Elle ne prononça pas un mot.

explain.fr: Not a + nom en tête : inversion.
explain.en: Not a + noun at the start: inversion.

say: Not a word did she utter.

question: Many ___ student has failed this exam.
fr: Bien des étudiants ont échoué à cet examen.

explain.fr: many a + nom singulier (littéraire) = bien des.
explain.en: many a + singular noun (literary) = many.

say: Many a student has failed this exam.

question: He spent what ___ money he had on books.
fr: Il a dépensé le peu d'argent qu'il avait en livres.

explain.fr: what little + indénombrable = le peu de… que.
explain.en: what little + uncountable = the small amount of… that.

say: He spent what little money he had on books.

question: He is not the man ___ he used to be.
fr: Il n'est plus l'homme qu'il était.

explain.fr: Attribut après be : that (who est possible, whom impossible).
explain.en: Complement after be: that.

say: He is not the man that he used to be.

question: She said nothing, ___ made matters worse.
fr: Elle n'a rien dit, ce qui a aggravé la situation.

explain.fr: , which reprend toute la proposition.
explain.en: , which refers back to the whole clause.

say: She said nothing, which made matters worse.

question: ___ wants to leave may do so now.
fr: Quiconque veut partir peut le faire maintenant.

explain.fr: whoever = quiconque.
explain.en: whoever = anyone who.

say: Whoever wants to leave may do so now.

question: You can invite ___ you like.
fr: Tu peux inviter qui tu veux.

explain.fr: Complément : whomever (soutenu) ; whoever est courant à l'oral.
explain.en: Object: whomever (formal); whoever is common in speech.

say: You can invite whomever you like.

question: The project was a success, ___ it was expensive.
fr: Le projet a été un succès, même s'il a coûté cher.

explain.fr: even though + proposition.
explain.en: even though + clause.

say: The project was a success, even though it was expensive.

question: ___ to popular belief, goldfish have good memories.
fr: Contrairement à une idée reçue, les poissons rouges ont une bonne mémoire.

explain.fr: contrary to + nom = contrairement à.
explain.en: contrary to + noun.

say: Contrary to popular belief, goldfish have good memories.

question: ___ his many faults, he was a generous man.
fr: Malgré tous ses défauts, c'était un homme généreux.

explain.fr: for all + nom = malgré (tous).
explain.en: for all + noun = despite.

say: For all his many faults, he was a generous man.

question: ___ as the evidence is, it does not prove his guilt.
fr: Si convaincantes que soient les preuves, elles ne prouvent pas sa culpabilité.

explain.fr: Adjectif + as + sujet + verbe = si… que.
explain.en: Adjective + as + subject + verb = however… it is.

say: Compelling as the evidence is, it does not prove his guilt.

question: He is wealthy, ___ not extravagantly so.
fr: Il est riche, quoique pas de façon extravagante.

explain.fr: though peut introduire un groupe sans verbe en fin de phrase.
explain.en: “Though” can introduce a verbless phrase.

say: He is wealthy, though not extravagantly so.

question: ___ as it was, the trip was worth it.
fr: Aussi fatigant qu'il ait été, le voyage en valait la peine.

explain.fr: Adjectif + as + it was = aussi… que.
explain.en: Adjective + as + it was = although it was…

say: Tiring as it was, the trip was worth it.

question: By the time the police arrive, the thieves ___.
fr: Le temps que la police arrive, les voleurs se seront enfuis.

explain.fr: Achèvement avant un moment futur : future perfect.
explain.en: Completion before a future time: future perfect.

say: By the time the police arrive, the thieves will have escaped.

question: I ___ you for ages! Where have you been?
fr: Ça fait une éternité que je ne t'ai pas vu ! Où étais-tu ?

explain.fr: for ages + situation jusqu'à maintenant : present perfect.
explain.en: “For ages” up to now: present perfect.

say: I haven't seen you for ages! Where have you been?

question: She ___ have been more pleased with the result.
fr: Elle n'aurait pas pu être plus contente du résultat.

explain.fr: couldn't have been more + adjectif = être on ne peut plus…
explain.en: couldn't have been more + adjective.

say: She couldn't have been more pleased with the result.

question: Little ___ he suspect what lay ahead.
fr: Il était loin de se douter de ce qui l'attendait.

explain.fr: Little en tête : inversion avec did.
explain.en: “Little” at the start: inversion with did.

say: Little did he suspect what lay ahead.

question: He was appointed ___ ambassador to Japan.
fr: Il a été nommé ambassadeur au Japon.

explain.fr: Fonction après appoint / elect / name : souvent sans article.
explain.en: Role after appoint / elect / name: often no article.

say: He was appointed ambassador to Japan.

question: ___ Smiths are coming to dinner.
fr: Les Smith viennent dîner.

explain.fr: Famille : the + nom au pluriel.
explain.en: Family: the + plural surname.

say: The Smiths are coming to dinner.

question: She has ___ remarkable ability to remember faces.
fr: Elle a une capacité remarquable à retenir les visages.

explain.fr: Nom abstrait qualifié : a + adjectif + nom.
explain.en: Qualified abstract noun: a + adjective + noun.

say: She has a remarkable ability to remember faces.

question: She is averse ___ taking risks.
fr: Elle répugne à prendre des risques.

explain.fr: averse to.
explain.en: averse to.

say: She is averse to taking risks.

question: The policy is tantamount ___ censorship.
fr: Cette politique équivaut à de la censure.

explain.fr: tantamount to = équivalent à.
explain.en: tantamount to.

say: The policy is tantamount to censorship.

question: He was absolved ___ all blame.
fr: Il a été lavé de tout reproche.

explain.fr: absolve of / from.
explain.en: absolve of.

say: He was absolved of all blame.

question: The plan is contingent ___ funding.
fr: Le plan dépend du financement.

explain.fr: contingent on / upon.
explain.en: contingent on.

say: The plan is contingent on funding.

question: She is impervious ___ criticism.
fr: Elle est insensible aux critiques.

explain.fr: impervious to.
explain.en: impervious to.

question: They acted in accordance ___ the rules.
fr: Ils ont agi conformément au règlement.

explain.fr: in accordance with.
explain.en: in accordance with.

say: They acted in accordance with the rules.

question: Were it not ___ the rain, we would have won.
fr: Sans la pluie, nous aurions gagné.

explain.fr: Were it not for = sans.
explain.en: Were it not for = without.

say: Were it not for the rain, we would have won.

question: So ___ was the crowd that the police had to intervene.
fr: La foule était si agitée que la police a dû intervenir.

explain.fr: So + adjectif + be + sujet.
explain.en: So + adjective + be + subject.

say: So unruly was the crowd that the police had to intervene.

question: Not only ___ the deadline, but they also exceeded the budget.
fr: Non seulement ils ont dépassé le délai, mais ils ont aussi dépassé le budget.

explain.fr: Not only en tête : inversion.
explain.en: Not only: inversion.

say: Not only did they miss the deadline, but they also exceeded the budget.

question: Such ___ the scale of the disaster that aid poured in from abroad.
fr: L'ampleur de la catastrophe était telle que l'aide afflua de l'étranger.

explain.fr: Such + be + sujet.
explain.en: Such + be + subject.

say: Such was the scale of the disaster that aid poured in from abroad.

question: It is imperative that the report ___ submitted by noon.
fr: Il est impératif que le rapport soit remis avant midi.

explain.fr: Subjonctif passif : be + participe.
explain.en: Passive subjunctive.

say: It is imperative that the report be submitted by noon.

question: The chairman proposed that the vote ___ postponed.
fr: Le président a proposé que le vote soit reporté.

explain.fr: propose that + be.
explain.en: propose that + be.

say: The chairman proposed that the vote be postponed.

question: I'd sooner you ___ mention it to anyone.
fr: Je préférerais que tu n'en parles à personne.

explain.fr: I'd sooner + autre sujet + prétérit.
explain.en: I'd sooner + past.

say: I'd sooner you didn't mention it to anyone.

question: It's high time the government ___ action.
fr: Il est grand temps que le gouvernement agisse.

explain.fr: It's high time + prétérit.
explain.en: It's high time + past.

say: It's high time the government took action.

question: You ___ well be right, but I'd like more evidence.
fr: Il est bien possible que vous ayez raison, mais j'aimerais plus de preuves.

explain.fr: may well.
explain.en: may well.

say: You may well be right, but I'd like more evidence.

question: She ___ have known about the plan; she was abroad.
fr: Elle ne pouvait pas être au courant du projet ; elle était à l'étranger.

explain.fr: couldn't have + participe.
explain.en: couldn't have.

say: She couldn't have known about the plan; she was abroad.

question: Try as I ___, I couldn't open the door.
fr: J'avais beau essayer, je n'arrivais pas à ouvrir la porte.

explain.fr: Try as I might = avoir beau essayer.
explain.en: Try as I might.

say: Try as I might, I couldn't open the door.

question: He was praised for ___ the crisis so effectively.
fr: Il a été salué pour avoir géré la crise si efficacement.

explain.fr: Préposition + having + participe.
explain.en: Preposition + having + participle.

say: He was praised for having handled the crisis so effectively.

question: I don't recall ___ consulted on the matter.
fr: Je ne me souviens pas avoir été consulté à ce sujet.

explain.fr: recall + being + participe (passif).
explain.en: recall + passive gerund.

say: I don't recall being consulted on the matter.

question: The building is said ___ in the twelfth century.
fr: On dit que le bâtiment a été construit au XIIe siècle.

explain.fr: Infinitif passif passé.
explain.en: Perfect passive infinitive.

say: The building is said to have been built in the twelfth century.

question: ___ all the evidence, the jury reached a verdict.
fr: Après avoir examiné toutes les preuves, le jury a rendu son verdict.

explain.fr: Having + participe = après avoir.
explain.en: Having + participle.

say: Having considered all the evidence, the jury reached a verdict.

question: She is not the woman ___ she was ten years ago.
fr: Elle n'est plus la femme qu'elle était il y a dix ans.

explain.fr: Attribut : that.
explain.en: Complement: that.

say: She is not the woman that she was ten years ago.

question: He gave us advice, most of ___ proved useful.
fr: Il nous a donné des conseils, dont la plupart se sont révélés utiles.

explain.fr: most of which.
explain.en: most of which.

say: He gave us advice, most of which proved useful.

question: ___ as the idea may seem, it actually works.
fr: Aussi absurde que paraisse l'idée, elle fonctionne.

explain.fr: Adjectif + as + sujet + verbe.
explain.en: Adjective + as + subject + verb.

say: Absurd as the idea may seem, it actually works.

question: He resigned, ___ admitting any wrongdoing.
fr: Il a démissionné sans reconnaître la moindre faute.

explain.fr: without + -ing.
explain.en: without + -ing.

say: He resigned, without admitting any wrongdoing.

question: The results were disappointing, ___ unexpected.
fr: Les résultats étaient décevants, voire inattendus.

explain.fr: if not = voire / sinon.
explain.en: if not.

say: The results were disappointing, if not unexpected.

question: Many ___ politician has made that promise.
fr: Bien des hommes politiques ont fait cette promesse.

explain.fr: many a + singulier (littéraire).
explain.en: many a + singular.

question:
Few would dispute that measurement can improve performance. Yet the historian Jerry Muller has argued that our obsession with quantifiable targets has become counterproductive. When hospitals are judged by mortality rates, some surgeons may decline to operate on high-risk patients; when schools are ranked by exam results, teachers may "teach to the test" at the expense of genuine learning. Such distortions illustrate what economists call Goodhart's law: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. Muller does not advocate abandoning metrics altogether, but rather using them judiciously, as aids to professional judgment rather than substitutes for it.

What is Muller's main argument?
fr: Lisez le texte, puis répondez : Quel est l'argument principal de Muller ?
answer: An obsession with targets has become counterproductive.

explain.fr: Réponse : « An obsession with targets has become counterproductive. ». Relisez le passage du texte qui en parle.
explain.en: Answer: “An obsession with targets has become counterproductive.”.

choices.t: An obsession with targets has become counterproductive.

Few would dispute that measurement can improve performance. Yet the historian Jerry Muller has argued that our obsession with quantifiable targets has become counterproductive. When hospitals are judged by mortality ___, some surgeons may decline to operate on high-risk patients; when schools are ranked by exam results, teachers may "teach to the test" at the expense of genuine learning. Such distortions illustrate what economists call Goodhart's law: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. Muller does not advocate abandoning metrics altogether, but rather using them judiciously, as aids to professional judgment rather than substitutes for it.

question:
Translators are often confronted with words that seem to have no equivalent in another language: the Portuguese "saudade", the German "Schadenfreude" or the Danish "hygge". Such terms are frequently cited as evidence that languages shape the way their speakers perceive the world. Yet the notion of strict untranslatability is somewhat misleading. A single word may lack a one-word counterpart, but its meaning can almost always be conveyed through a phrase or a paraphrase. The real challenge for translators lies less in individual words than in connotation, rhythm and cultural allusion, which resist neat transfer from one language to another.

question:
Advances in genetic engineering have raised the startling possibility of bringing extinct species back to life. Projects to resurrect the woolly mammoth or the passenger pigeon have captured the public imagination. Proponents contend that de-extinction could restore lost ecosystems and atone for damage caused by humans. Skeptics, however, warn that the vast sums involved would be better spent protecting the many species currently on the brink. They also caution that a resurrected animal, lacking the knowledge passed down by its ancestors and the habitat they once occupied, might be little more than a curiosity, a living exhibit rather than a genuine member of a functioning ecosystem.

What has genetic engineering made possible, according to the text?

explain.fr: Réponse : « Potentially bringing extinct species back ». Relisez le passage du texte qui en parle.
explain.en: Answer: “Potentially bringing extinct species back”.

question:
Once regarded as a medical disorder, a kind of homesickness that could prove fatal to soldiers far from home, nostalgia has undergone a remarkable rehabilitation. Psychologists now view it as a largely positive emotion that strengthens our sense of identity and connection to others. Recalling cherished memories, research suggests, can counteract loneliness and boost optimism about the future. Nevertheless, nostalgia has a darker side when it is collective rather than personal. Political movements frequently invoke an idealized past, a golden age that may never have existed, to justify resistance to change. The emotion that comforts individuals can thus be harnessed to mislead societies.

How was nostalgia regarded in the past?

explain.fr: Réponse : « As a medical disorder ». Relisez le passage du texte qui en parle.
explain.en: Answer: “As a medical disorder”.

title: Nostalgia

question:
Once regarded as a medical disorder, a kind of homesickness that could prove fatal to soldiers far from home, nostalgia has undergone a remarkable rehabilitation. Psychologists now view it as a largely positive emotion that strengthens our sense of identity and connection to others. Recalling cherished memories, research suggests, can counteract loneliness and boost optimism about the future. Nevertheless, nostalgia has a darker side when it is collective rather than personal. Political movements frequently invoke an idealized past, a golden age that may never have existed, to justify resistance to change. The emotion that comforts individuals can thus be harnessed to mislead societies.

answer: Collective nostalgia can be used to resist change and mislead.

question:
Many of us pride ourselves on our ability to multitask, answering emails during meetings or texting while watching television. Neuroscience, however, offers a sobering verdict: the brain does not really perform demanding tasks simultaneously but switches rapidly between them, incurring a cost each time. These "switch costs" may seem trivial, but they accumulate, reducing efficiency and increasing errors. Paradoxically, heavy multitaskers appear to be worse at filtering out irrelevant information than those who tend to focus on one thing at a time. The implication is clear, if unwelcome: doing less at once may allow us to accomplish more overall.

What does neuroscience say about multitasking?

answer: The brain switches rapidly between tasks rather than doing them simultaneously.

question:
It is tempting to think of music as a succession of sounds, but composers have long understood that silence is equally integral to their art. A well-placed pause can heighten tension, draw attention to what follows or allow a phrase to resonate. The American composer John Cage took this idea to its logical extreme in a piece in which the performer plays nothing at all for four and a half minutes. Far from being a joke, the work invites listeners to notice the ambient sounds around them, the coughs, the rustling programs, the hum of the building, and thereby questions the very boundary between music and noise.

What do composers understand about silence?

answer: It is as integral to music as sound.

question:
Governments increasingly rely on "nudges", subtle changes to the way choices are presented, to steer citizens toward better decisions. Placing fruit at eye level in school canteens, or making pension enrollment the default option, can shift behavior dramatically without banning anything or imposing new taxes. Advocates describe this approach as "libertarian paternalism": people remain free to choose, yet the choice architecture gently favors outcomes that serve their long-term interests. Critics, however, detect something insidious in policies that work precisely because people do not notice them. A state that manipulates rather than persuades, they argue, treats its citizens less as rational agents than as objects to be managed, and its benevolence today is no guarantee against abuse tomorrow.

question:
The novel, now so familiar that we scarcely think of it as a form at all, was once regarded with considerable suspicion. In the eighteenth century, moralists warned that it inflamed the passions of impressionable readers, particularly young women, and distracted them from more improving pursuits. What made the form so troubling was perhaps also what made it so compelling: its capacity to render the inner life of ordinary people with unprecedented intimacy. Unlike epic or tragedy, which dealt with gods and kings, the novel concerned itself with clerks, servants and governesses, and invited readers to inhabit their thoughts. In doing so, some historians contend, it may have helped to foster the very capacity for empathy on which modern notions of human rights depend.

How was the novel regarded in the eighteenth century?

explain.fr: Réponse : « With considerable suspicion ». Relisez le passage du texte qui en parle.
explain.en: Answer: “With considerable suspicion”.

question:
We tend to admire experts whose judgments seem instantaneous: the chess master who sees the winning move at a glance, the firefighter who senses that a floor is about to collapse. Such intuition, research suggests, is not mysterious but the product of thousands of hours of feedback, which allow the mind to recognize patterns it cannot consciously articulate. Yet intuition is only as reliable as the environment in which it was formed. In domains where outcomes are regular and feedback is swift, expert hunches can be remarkably accurate. In domains that are noisy or unpredictable, such as long-term political forecasting, confident experts often fare little better than chance, and their certainty may be more dangerous than useful.

answer: The product of long experience and feedback
